events.headline: Houthi Missile Strike on Yemen Training Camp Death Toll Revised Up to 73, Deadliest of War's New Phase
events.summary: The toll from the October 19 Houthi ballistic missile strike on the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre in Shabwa, Yemen was revised upward to 73 killed, with over 200 wounded and 14 missing. Victims were mostly recruits aged 18-20 for a new 'Rapid Intervention' force; it is the deadliest single strike since Yemen's civil war resumed roughly three months ago.

events.headline: Brazil's Lula-Bolsonaro Runoff Remains Razor-Thin With Markets Still Favoring Bolsonaro
events.summary: Ahead of the Oct 25 presidential runoff, polls show an extremely tight race with Flavio Bolsonaro holding a modest edge over Lula, roughly 51-49 in most surveys, though results vary. Prediction markets gave Bolsonaro a 77-79% implied win probability as of Oct 24.

events.headline: Saudi Arabia Postpones Flagship FII Investment Conference to 2027 Citing Security Situation
events.summary: Saudi Arabia postponed its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference, originally scheduled for October 26-29, to 2027, citing the security situation following Houthi missile attacks including the Riyadh airport strike. The airport has remained closed; scheduled speakers included Jamie Dimon, Jane Fraser, David Solomon and Larry Fink.

events.headline: Ethiopian Forces Advance to Zalambessa Border Town With Tanks Amid Eritrea War Fears
events.summary: Ethiopian troops backed by tanks have advanced to Zalambessa on the border with Eritrea, raising fears of renewed war between the two countries. Drone strikes reportedly hit Eritrean vehicles near Adi Grat as tensions escalate along the frontier.

events.headline: Abyei Market Drone Strike Death Toll Climbs to 150-220 as Sudan Blames RSF Fuel Targeting
events.summary: The death toll from a drone strike on the Amiet market in the disputed Abyei area has risen to between 150 and 220 people, among the deadliest single attacks in the region's recent conflict. Sudanese military officials say the Rapid Support Forces targeted a fuel depot at the market, causing mass civilian casualties.

events.headline: Putin Agrees to Resume Trilateral Ukraine Peace Talks, Releases Detained American
events.summary: Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on October 21, during which Russia released American Stephen Hubbard, detained since 2022. A US official said Russia and Ukraine agreed to resume trilateral technical peace talks after November 10.

events.headline: Magnitude 7.0 Earthquake Kills at Least 16 in Tibet's Baqen County
events.summary: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Baqen County in Nagqu, Tibet, at 22:33 local time on October 22, killing at least 16 people and injuring over 50. The quake collapsed more than 339 homes, prompting deployment of over 1,600 rescuers.

events.headline: DRC's Kabila-M23 FRN Coalition Names Leaders as Fighting Spreads to Uvira, South Kivu
events.summary: The Kabila-aligned FRN coalition with M23 named its leadership, including Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa and Sultani Makenga as vice presidents. Fighting has spread from Walungu into the Ruzizi Plain and Uvira district of South Kivu, with government-coalition forces reportedly losing positions in the Bijombo highlands after drone strikes, materializing earlier warnings of a 'general attack.'

events.headline: Attacks on Shipping in Strait of Hormuz Surge to Wartime High
events.summary: Attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz hit a wartime high in October, with about 27 attacks recorded this month according to IMO figures. Oil flow through the strait has fallen to roughly 68% of its pre-war baseline, about 11.6 million barrels per day versus 17.1 million.

events.headline: UN Warns Taiz, Yemen Could Run Out of Wheat Within Weeks as Houthi Siege Tightens
events.summary: The UN warns that wheat and flour supplies in Taiz could run out within three weeks after Houthi forces tightened their blockade by seizing the city's last main road link to other areas. Food prices have risen about 50%, more than 600,000 people including 200,000+ children depend on aid, and medical supplies are nearing depletion.

events.headline: Russian Strikes on Ukrainian Energy Grid Kill 8, Cut Power to Over 500,000
events.summary: Russian strikes on energy facilities across six to nine Ukrainian regions overnight on Oct 22-23 killed at least 8 people and wounded 67, cutting power to more than 500,000 residents. A drone strike on the Lviv region left about 175 settlements without electricity after a DTEK thermal plant halted generation.

events.headline: Islamic State-Linked Fighters Kill at Least 48 Civilians Near Menaka, Eastern Mali
events.summary: On October 18, fighters from the Islamic State Sahel Province (ISSP) raided Idaksahak pastoralist communities near Menaka, killing at least 48 civilians. The attack was reportedly carried out in retaliation for suspected informants aiding a Malian army drone strike.

events.headline: Nigeria Confirms Bundibugyo Ebola Strain Matches DRC Outbreak, 44 Contacts Monitored
events.summary: Nigerian health officials confirmed on Oct 20 that the imported Ebola case matches the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain from the DRC outbreak that began in May 2026, marking the first spread of that outbreak to West Africa. Forty-four contacts have been identified and are under monitoring.

events.headline: El Salvador Forces Clash With Haitian Gangs in Rescue Bid for Four Abducted Soldiers
events.summary: Four Salvadoran aviation technicians supporting Haiti's UN-backed Gang Suppression Force were abducted by gangs on Oct 18 near Port-au-Prince. President Bukele deployed about 200 special forces on Oct 22 in a rescue operation; clashes killed at least 7 gang members and wounded 4 GSF personnel, while the hostages' fate remained unconfirmed as of Oct 24.

events.headline: France Bans Protests in Lyon, Marseille and Extends Curfews After 2,700 Detained in Riots
events.summary: France outright banned protests in Lyon and Marseille and extended curfews in central Paris after unrest left about 2,700 people in custody, up from over 1,000 earlier. Some 70,000 security personnel have been deployed nationwide, and President Macron blamed 'seditious' far-left groups for the violence.

events.headline: South Korea Calls for Military Talks as North Korea Presses Ahead With Border Loudspeakers
events.summary: South Korea's military formally called on Oct 23 for inter-Korean military talks to resolve disputes over the exact border location and prevent accidental clashes. The appeal comes as North Korea, under Kim Yo-jong's earlier warning, presses ahead with plans to reactivate propaganda loudspeakers along the DMZ.

events.headline: 150,000 Rally in Belgrade in Final Push Before Serbia's Oct. 25 Election
events.summary: Around 150,000 people rallied in Belgrade on October 21-22, the final demonstration by the student-backed opposition before Sunday's election. Civil society groups warned the election environment falls short of free-and-fair standards.

events.headline: Israeli Strikes Kill More Palestinians in Gaza as Death Toll Since Ceasefire Nears 1,500
events.summary: On October 22, Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four Palestinians in Gaza City, Khan Younis, and near Jabalia. Health officials say roughly 1,500 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began, while Israel reports four soldiers killed in the same period.

events.headline: Israel-Lebanon Talks in Tampa End Without Deal as Israeli Strikes Intensify in South Lebanon
events.summary: Two days of US-mediated Israel-Lebanon military talks at CENTCOM headquarters in Tampa ended on October 22 without a breakthrough on Hezbollah disarmament verification. Israeli strikes and demolitions escalated in south Lebanon, hitting Kfar Tebnit and other villages.

events.headline: CENTCOM Marks 100 Days of Naval Blockade on Iran as IRGC Maintains Hormuz Closure
events.summary: US CENTCOM marked 100 days of its naval blockade of Iranian ports on October 22, saying it has blocked roughly $25 billion in Iranian crude exports. Iran's IRGC had earlier declared the Strait of Hormuz closed "until US conditions are met" and warned of strikes on US-escorted vessels.

events.headline: Russia Strikes Kyiv With Three Waves of Ballistic Missiles Hours After Witkoff-Putin Meeting
events.summary: Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles plus drones at Kyiv overnight on October 21-22 in three waves, killing one person and injuring up to 24. The attack damaged an ambulance station, a monastery, and metro bridge infrastructure, coming hours after US envoy Steve Witkoff met Putin in St. Petersburg.

events.headline: Student Protests Spread Across Indonesia as Worst Regional Haze in a Decade Persists
events.summary: More than 500 protesters gathered outside the Central Kalimantan governor's office on Oct 23 demanding a national haze emergency declaration. Indonesia's health ministry reports over 333,000 acute respiratory illness cases across seven provinces since mid-August amid Southeast Asia's worst haze in a decade.

events.headline: Hurricane Vance Strengthens to Category 2, Could Hit Category 3 Near Mexico's Pacific Coast
events.summary: Hurricane Vance intensified to Category 2 strength (105 mph) on Oct 23 roughly 425 miles south-southwest of Acapulco. The US National Hurricane Center forecasts possible strengthening to Category 3 as it tracks toward the Puerto Vallarta area by Oct 27, making it the seventh major Pacific hurricane of the 2026 season.

events.headline: Israel Locks Down West Bank After Hebron Checkpoint Attack Kills Two Soldiers
events.summary: Two Palestinian gunmen attacked a checkpoint near Hebron on Oct 23, killing Israeli soldiers Ron Yonatan Roytman, 23, and Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, and wounding three others before being killed themselves. Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered Hebron sealed and a full West Bank closure, calling for an intensified military campaign.

events.headline: US Orders Non-Essential Staff Out of Riyadh Embassy Citing Iran/Houthi Threat Intelligence
events.summary: The US State Department ordered the mandatory departure of non-essential personnel and families from its Riyadh embassy, citing intelligence of 'advanced-stage' plots against US officials linked to Houthi and Iran tensions. The department disputed broader reports that the drawdown also covers the UAE, Qatar, Jordan and Bahrain, saying the order applies only to Saudi Arabia.

events.headline: Malaysia Deregisters Opposition Bloc Perikatan Nasional Ahead of Malacca Election
events.summary: Malaysian authorities deregistered the opposition coalition Perikatan Nasional weeks before a state election in Malacca, dealing a blow to rivals of Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. The move is likely to reshape the opposition landscape heading into the vote.

events.headline: Rubio Urges Cubans to Secretly Work With CIA as Trump Floats Sending Him to Negotiate
events.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Oct 23 urged Cubans seeking political change to discreetly partner with the CIA, while President Trump said Washington would 'take care of Cuba' and might send Rubio to finalize a deal. Cuban officials condemned the remarks as the CIA posted Spanish-language instructions for contacting the agency.

events.headline: Ramaphosa Warns South Africa to Prepare for Possible Loss of US AGOA Trade Access
events.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa warned the country must prepare for the potential loss of duty-free access to the US market under the African Growth and Opportunity Act. The warning comes amid strained US-South Africa relations and uncertainty over the trade program's renewal.

events.headline: Report: Musk Ordered Starlink Slowdown That Disrupted Ukraine's Drone Operations
events.summary: A Wall Street Journal report cited by multiple outlets says Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of Starlink satellite service that disrupted Ukrainian military drone operations, blindsiding Kyiv. US lawmakers have launched an investigation into the disruptions.

events.headline: Thousands of Venezuelans Join First Nationwide Opposition Protest in Nearly Two Years
events.summary: Thousands demonstrated nationwide on October 22 in the first country-wide opposition protest in nearly two years, organized by Maria Corina Machado's Vente Venezuela. Protesters demanded a 2027 election date, Machado's return, and the release of political prisoners.

events.headline: Burkina Faso's Parliament Unanimously Votes to Reinstate the Death Penalty
events.summary: Burkina Faso's transitional parliament voted unanimously to reinstate the death penalty, reversing its 2018 abolition. The move, backed by military ruler Ibrahim Traore's government, comes amid an ongoing jihadist insurgency and crackdown on crime.

events.headline: Ukraine Launches One of Its Largest Drone Attacks of the War on Moscow Region, 630 UAVs Tracked
events.summary: Russia reported tracking roughly 630 Ukrainian drones in one of the largest single attacks on the Moscow region since the war began, with casualties and damage reported. The strike adds to an escalating pattern of long-range drone exchanges between the two sides.

events.headline: Eight Inmates Killed in Simultaneous Ecuador Prison Riots as Opposition Candidate Jailed
events.summary: Near-simultaneous riots on Oct 22 at Cotopaxi No. 1 prison in Latacunga and El Inca prison in Quito killed eight inmates and injured about ten. Separately, a judge ordered pretrial detention for leftist presidential candidate Luisa Gonzalez in a $500,000 money-laundering case tied to her 2023 campaign; any link between the two events is unconfirmed.

events.headline: Heavy Gunfire Near US Embassy in Tabarre, Haiti Prompts Lockdown
events.summary: The US Embassy in Port-au-Prince issued a security alert after sustained gunfire broke out near the Tabarre bridge amid a Haitian police gang-suppression operation in Tabarre and Cite Soleil. Embassy staff were ordered to shelter in place as fighting continued in the area.

events.headline: Argentine Bond Selloff Deepens as IMF Cuts 2026 Growth Forecast to 2.1%
events.summary: Argentine sovereign bonds extended losses as the IMF slashed its 2026 growth forecast for the country to 2.1%, citing election-related uncertainty. The selloff reflects growing investor concern ahead of upcoming elections and continuing fiscal pressures.

events.headline: Pakistan, Turkey, Qatar, Indonesia Sign 'Badr' Defense Cooperation Pact in Doha
events.summary: Turkey, Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia signed the "Badr" memorandum of understanding in Doha on October 21, deepening defense-industry cooperation. The pact includes provisions for joint production and technology transfers among the four nations.

events.headline: Bangladesh Dengue Death Toll Reaches 357 Amid Nationwide Outbreak and Measles Crisis
events.summary: Bangladesh's dengue outbreak has killed 357 people nationwide, with health officials citing treatment delays as deaths continue to mount. The dengue surge comes alongside a separate measles crisis straining the country's healthcare system.

events.headline: Mexico Charges Former Chihuahua Prosecutor With Treason Over US Agents' Role in Drug Raid
events.summary: Mexican authorities have charged a former Chihuahua state prosecutor with treason, a rarely used charge, over allegations he allowed US law enforcement agents to participate directly in a drug raid on Mexican soil. The case underscores rising sensitivity over US security involvement inside Mexico.

events.headline: Venezuela Government-Opposition Talks Agree to Review Four Political Laws
events.summary: Venezuela's interim government and opposition concluded a third round of talks on October 21, agreeing to review four laws including the Comptroller General's powers, seen as a precursor to lifting Machado's political ban.

events.headline: El Nino Rains Flood Piura Region in Northern Peru, Threatening 1.2 Million Residents
events.summary: Torrential rains linked to a coastal El Nino have flooded streets in Piura and Chulucanas, northern Peru, submerging neighborhoods and raising dengue risk. Authorities have urged evacuations in areas at risk of river overflow, with up to 1.2 million residents potentially affected.

events.headline: Armed Group Clashes Trap About 400 Civilians in Narino, Colombia; Aid Convoy Attacked
events.summary: Fighting between dissident FARC factions and self-defense groups in Linares and Los Andes, Narino, has trapped roughly 400 civilians, prompting evacuations of over 300 people. A humanitarian convoy attempting to reach the area was attacked, and Colombia's Ombudsman's Office has called for urgent assistance to stranded communities.

events.headline: Europe Records Highest-Ever West Nile Virus Season With 1,855 Cases, 141 Deaths
events.summary: The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reported a record 2026 West Nile virus season across Europe, with 1,855 cases and 141 deaths, and the virus spreading to new areas. Italy has been among the hardest-hit countries.

events.headline: Houthi Drone Debris Kills Two at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah Oil Field
events.summary: Falling debris from a Houthi drone attack killed two people and injured two others at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province. The strike marks an escalation of Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure.

events.headline: Libya's Eastern Parliament Ratifies Turkey Maritime Deal, Egypt and Greece Reject It
events.summary: Libya's eastern, Haftar-aligned House of Representatives ratified a 2019 Turkey-Libya maritime memorandum on Oct 20-21, reviving a dispute with Egypt, Greece and Cyprus over eastern Mediterranean rights. Greece called it a breach of international law, Egypt declared it null and void, and Turkey's foreign minister said conditions were 'ripe' for Libyan east-west reunification.

events.headline: China's Economy Grows 4.5% in Q3, Beating Forecasts
events.summary: China's National Bureau of Statistics reported Q3 GDP growth of 4.5% year-on-year, up from 4.3% in Q2, beating forecasts, with cumulative growth of 4.6% for the first three quarters of 2026. Growth was driven by exports and high-tech manufacturing despite sluggish domestic consumption.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Forces Suffer Heavy Losses in Renewed Assault on Ngapyi Island
events.summary: Myanmar's military junta suffered heavy casualties in a renewed amphibious assault on Ngapyi Island in Rakhine State's Pauktaw Township. The battle marks an escalation in fighting between junta forces and resistance groups in the region.

events.headline: Pakistani Forces, Afghan Taliban Trade Fire Along Kurram-Paktia Border Amid Stalled Talks
events.summary: Pakistani forces and Taliban fighters exchanged roughly four hours of artillery fire on Oct 17 along the Kurram-Paktia border, with a rocket striking a residential area in Pewar. Casualty claims are sharply disputed - Afghan-aligned media report seven Pakistani soldiers killed while Pakistan-aligned media claim 13 TTP fighters killed - as Russia and the EU urged de-escalation after inconclusive talks in Moscow.

events.headline: Typhoon Champi Toll in Taiwan Rises to 527 Injured, Over 167,000 Homes Lost Power
events.summary: Typhoon Champi's toll in Taiwan has risen to one dead and 527 injured, up from earlier partial tallies, with more than 167,000 homes losing power and over 4,300 people evacuated. The storm has weakened as it moves on toward Okinawa.

events.headline: Italy's Truckers Ease Diesel-Price Protests After Government Approves Aid Decree
events.summary: Truckers and farmers who had blockaded Calabria's ports and airports since mid-October over diesel costs suspended their protests after Prime Minister Meloni's government approved a decree adding 106 million euros in tax credits plus farming and fishing aid. Drivers warned they could resume action if an Oct 27 meeting with Transport Minister Salvini fails.

events.headline: Second Australian Lawmaker's Office Threatened Days After Car-Attack on Fellow MP
events.summary: A man entered Western Australian minister Hannah Beazley's Perth office on October 21 wielding wood and screaming, days after federal MP Helen Haines had both legs amputated following a deliberate car-attack in an unrelated incident. No link between the two incidents has been found.

events.headline: Washington National Guard Member Shot in Barracks Row Altercation; Suspect Charged
events.summary: A National Guard member intervening in a fight was shot on October 18 by a suspect who pointed a gun at him; the Guardsman returned fire, wounding the suspect. The suspect was charged with federal crimes on October 21.

events.headline: Peshawar High Court Adjourns Challenge to KP Governor's Rule to November 10
events.summary: The Peshawar High Court heard initial arguments on October 20 in petitions challenging Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's governor's rule, imposed on October 11. A two-judge bench issued notices to respondents and adjourned the case to November 10.

events.headline: Argentine Judge Dismisses Fraud Probe Into Milei Over $LIBRA Meme-Coin Collapse
events.summary: Federal Judge Martinez De Giorgi dismissed the criminal fraud investigation into President Milei and his sister Karina over the February 2025 collapse of the $LIBRA memecoin, ruling the events did not constitute a criminal offense. A parallel probe into promoter Hayden Davis was also dismissed.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Airstrikes Kill Civilians in Pauktaw Township, Rakhine State
events.summary: Myanmar junta aircraft carried out nighttime airstrikes on October 21-22 on Pauktaw town and nearby villages in Rakhine State, killing at least two civilians and injuring six. The strikes are part of an ongoing junta bombing campaign against Arakan Army-held areas.

events.headline: Thousands Protest Across Poland on Sixth Anniversary of Near-Total Abortion Ban
events.summary: Thousands marched in Warsaw and more than 20 other Polish cities on the sixth anniversary of the Constitutional Tribunal's near-total abortion ban under the slogan 'Red card for abortion.' The protests came days after parliament passed two liberalizing bills expected to face a presidential veto from Karol Nawrocki.

events.headline: Colombia Seizes Record 7.6 Tonnes of Cocaine at Cartagena Port
events.summary: Colombian police, with US DEA support, seized 7.6 tonnes of cocaine hidden in panela sugar bound for the Netherlands at Cartagena port on October 21, the country's largest bust in a decade. Two Dutch nationals were arrested in connection with the shipment.

events.headline: Philippine Peso Hits 31st Record Low of 2026 at P63.615 per Dollar
events.summary: The Philippine peso closed at a fresh record low of 63.615 to the US dollar on Oct 23, its 31st record low this year. The decline was driven by elevated oil prices, September inflation of 7.2%, and broader dollar strength amid geopolitical tension.

events.headline: Houthis Strike Aden and Mukalla Airports With Ballistic Missiles
events.summary: On October 21, Houthi forces fired ballistic missiles near Aden International Airport, Mukalla's al-Rayyan Airport, and a factory in Taiz. The Houthis said they targeted a coalition operations room at Badr Camp; no deaths were confirmed, in an attack distinct from the deadlier Shabwa training-camp strike.

events.headline: Two Syrian Security Officers Killed in Raid on ISIL Cell Near Damascus
events.summary: Syrian security forces raided a suspected ISIL cell in Rankous on October 22, resulting in the deaths of two security personnel and five wounded. Five alleged ISIL members were killed in the raid and six others were arrested.

events.headline: Milei Pursues Falklands Oil Diplomacy in Madrid Amid Argentine Bond Selloff
events.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei said in Madrid on October 22 that Argentina would pursue recovery of the Falklands diplomatically amid a dispute with the UK over the Sea Lion oil project, with a Hamburg tribunal hearing set for November 10. Argentine bond yields approached 12% amid election-related risk.

events.headline: South African Constitutional Court Forces Ballot Reprint Ahead of Nov. 4 Elections
events.summary: South Africa's Constitutional Court ordered the electoral commission to reinstate 181 ANC candidates excluded from the November 4 municipal elections. The ruling forced a rush ballot reprint across six municipalities ahead of the vote.

events.headline: Colombia Extradites FARC-Dissident Front 33 Leader 'Mocho Olmedo' to United States
events.summary: Willington Henao Gutierrez, alias 'Mocho Olmedo' and second-in-command of the FARC-dissident Front 33, was extradited on Oct 23 to face US drug-trafficking and money-laundering charges in a Florida federal court. Six other Colombians were extradited in the same action.

events.headline: Colombian Army Black Hawk Crashes in Cauca; All 19 Aboard Survive, Last 13 Rescued
events.summary: A Colombian Army UH-60 Black Hawk helicopter crashed on October 19 near Inza, Cauca, carrying 19 personnel, all of whom survived. Thirteen soldiers stranded in forested terrain were evacuated on October 21-22.

events.headline: Canada and Ontario Unveil C$8.7 Billion Package for Steel, Auto and Critical Minerals
events.summary: Canadian PM Mark Carney and Ontario Premier Doug Ford announced a C$8.7 billion federal-provincial package on October 21 to counter US tariffs. The funding covers steel production, auto-sector retooling, and critical minerals infrastructure.

events.headline: Four Police Killed in Gunbattle in Karak, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
events.summary: Four police personnel, including a CTD deputy superintendent, were killed in a gunbattle on October 22 after raiding an alleged militant commander's house in Karak. Two militants were also killed in the operation.

events.headline: Senegal's 72-Hour General Strike Disrupts Healthcare, Schools, Transport Before Youth Olympics
events.summary: Senegal's Trade Union Front, representing 13 unions, led a 72-hour general strike from Oct 21-23 over wages, pensions and labor codes, disrupting hospitals, schools and Dakar's bus network, prompting a military deployment to maintain minimal transit service. The action came days before Dakar hosts the Youth Olympic Games opening Oct 31; the government called the strike unlawful.

events.headline: Mexico's IMSS Healthcare Workers Protest Despite 8% Pay Raise Offer
events.summary: IMSS and the SNTSS union agreed to an 8% pay raise on October 21, but healthcare workers protested in Mexico City demanding a 10% raise and the removal of union leader Rafael Olivos. The dispute highlights ongoing tension between rank-and-file workers and union leadership.

events.headline: Chile Declares Red Alert as New Storm Floods Santiago Metropolitan Region
events.summary: Chile's disaster agency SENAPRED declared a red alert on October 20 for the Metropolitan Region ahead of a storm bringing heavy rain and hail. Flooding hit Maipu and Padre Hurtado, and evacuations occurred in Puente Alto.

events.headline: Historic Delhi Mosque Near PM Modi's Residence Served Six-Day Eviction Notice
events.summary: India's Land and Development Office declared the century-old, heritage-listed Race Course Mosque 'unauthorised' on Oct 19 and ordered it vacated within six days, after its electricity and water had been cut on Oct 7. The Delhi Waqf Board disputes the order, citing a 1977 gazette notification recognizing the site's Waqf status.

events.headline: 17 Sugar Mill Workers Abducted on Indus Highway in Dera Ismail Khan
events.summary: Armed men linked to the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan set up a checkpoint on the Indus Highway near Cheera Minor overnight on October 20-21, abducting 17 people including eight sugar mill workers. Five hostages were later released, and the Counter Terrorism Department has registered a case against the TTP.

events.headline: Chile Renews $7.5 Billion Currency Swap Line With China for Five More Years
events.summary: Chile's central bank renewed its precautionary roughly $7.5 billion renminbi-peso swap agreement with the People's Bank of China, in place since 2015, for another five years, the bank announced on Oct 23.
